title: Buddy Bolden's loud trumpet and Carnish
summary: Bolden's volume and style, Carnish on trombone, and instruments left in the pool room.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

You understand? About to jump out with him, you know? That's why these guys in the prison all of them talking about. They're there with papas. Tony, I'm a Rick and all of them.

Sure, that's right. You were telling us about the bowling. You were a boy when you heard bowling. Can you remember anything about him? I didn't even know recording with Buddy Bowling. No, I know. I mean did you hear him play? Oh sure, I heard Buddy Bowling.
Used to go back to, had the economy hall there. Not the economy hall there, Mason's Hall right? On the David Street then? I used to go to Buddy Bowling. Buddy Bowling. Buddy Bowling.
Buddy Bowling was one of the heaviest, loudest trumpet players that ever was in New Orleans. Him and Carnish. Carnish was an old friend of mine with a carnish. How did Carnish play trombone?
Is he really good on it or not so good?
No, he never was no musician. He just had a good ear. That's all. He's good ear. He knew the air screen. He knew the instrument all right.
He knew the instrument all right.

He knew the instrument. A good ear. And a good fella to get along with. He was, he and Buddy Bowling and them used to play the gap. So when Buddy would play his trumpet and he'd take that dirt, which is what the people are known nowadays. He used to wear a doi be all the time in the street. That was a style. It's like what Sharky is doing now. I can tell you plenty about old Sharky too. It's like Buddy Bowling is the way that doi be in the street. And he'd leave him with his horn all the time. Buddy Bowling. Every time you see Buddy Bowling, Buddy Bowling happens on it. He's in the pool room anyway. So you could leave your instrument in the pool room in them days. And Ben Mulliken's place was packed and jammed with instruments. With basses and drums. You had to take him on the street because he had no automobiles. That's right. Take him on the street. Everybody pile the drums up in the corner. And nobody touched nothing. You leave your corner on the counter. Tell the bartender to take it. Take it. You just put it back. You tumble everything. Nobody takes nothing. You can walk New Orleans from Jackson Barrett up to the protection levee. No pulleys from nothing wouldn't stop it. But you can't do that nowadays. So Buddy Bowling was a fellow who always had his corner. He'd pull out in the bar rooms and play. And him and his do everything. And he'd get drunk like that. So Buddy was the loudest corner player we ever had in the city of New Orleans. But come down to playing sweet and waltzes with nobody in the country. He played something on the art of Wayne King. He was one of the sweetest trumpet players on waltzes and things like that. And the old slow blues. Buddy Bowling made them women jump out the window. The old slow lowdown blues. He had a moan in his corner that looked like it goes all through you. It's like you're in a church or something. I don't know. But that's just what everybody was crazy about Buddy Bowling when he blew a wall. A shouters. A shouters. See. And them old lowdown blues. And he was the sweetest trumpet player in the world. Poor boy went crazy. He died about eight years ago. Yeah. That's wonderful. One of them. And he'd tell his boys to get low. And he'd say get low. And he'd take it. And women would be jumping out the window. Jumping around. Howling. Buddy Bowling. Buddy Bowling. It's no corner player yet that had a tone with Buddy Bowling had when he played slow. And he had. I don't understand it. Nobody yet. No other trumpet player can tell you. Louie Armstrong or Joe Oliver. None of them. That Louie the only one living. Me and him always was together like that. You know. To him this place. We all come up. None of them had a tone like Buddy Bowling. Where he found those kind of things to put in the blues. Old river. Old levy camp and all that. They just make. Like a. It's like a spiritual feeling goes through you. But what he puts in it nobody knows. And he had a cup. You know. A special made cup. He make that tone and I'm telling you. Moon. Just like a preacher is preaching a Baptist preacher. Yeah. He's really wonderful. And the walls. He could play sweet. He could play this as sweet as he could play loud. He could. He's wonderful. That'd be like a drinking cup. A cup you drink out of.
